title: Ask a testable question
brief: Define what the initial pitch experiment must establish. Choose a measurable response and an inclusive success threshold.
supplied: 900 kg trainer; rho=1.20 kg/m³; V=20 m/s; S=27.25 m²; c=4 m; usable dCm=0.153; Iy=5000 kg m²; other=-750 N m; target=0.12 rad/s². Nose-up moment is positive about the declared CG.
Available and required moment (N m), margin (N m), acceleration (rad/s²).

Hold the supplied usable coefficient increment, loading, flap/power state, and local-flow assumption fixed during this first screen. Full available nose-up control moment is commanded. These assumptions require later review.
This is a bounded teaching calculation. It does not establish aircraft safety, successful takeoff, or behavior outside the specified condition.
Increasing speed increases available moment quadratically.
Available 4002.48 N m; required 1350 N m; margin 2652.48 N m; full-command acceleration 0.650496 rad/s².
Test 20 and 10 m/s, include equality with the required acceleration.
Show controls with units, supplied and student results separately, a result trace, and a clear limitation.

For each speed, compute available moment, subtract the 1350 N m demand, and calculate (available-750)/5000. For the short replay only, pitch angle=0.5*initialAcceleration*time² from rest over 0.5 s. This extrapolation is not a ground-run simulation.
The supplied baseline meets initial authority demand. No takeoff claim follows.

fields.label: Write the engineering question
fields.help: Include 20 m/s, the elevator, initial pitch acceleration, and the at-least 0.12 rad/s² requirement. Ask whether the demand can be met; do not assert the result.

fields.label: Measured response
fields.help: Choose the statement supported by the supplied condition, then justify it in your reasoning.

fields.label: Required acceleration (rad/s²)
fields.help: Enter a number only; use the unit in the label. Accepted absolute error: ±0.0001. Keep the sign; enter ratios as fractions, not percentages.

fields.label: Success criterion
fields.help: Choose the statement supported by the supplied condition, then justify it in your reasoning.

fields.label: Explain your engineering reasoning
fields.help: Use your own words. Refer to the condition, a quantity with units, and the limit of your claim. Written reasoning awaits instructor review.

Use the specified response demand, not the observed capacity.

checks.expected: Initial pitch response at the stated condition
checks.message: This model only addresses the initial pitch response. Narrow a takeoff or safety question before proceeding.

hints: Name the response this model actually calculates. It has no takeoff-distance or crosswind model.
State the operating condition and 0.12 rad/s² demand in your question.
At least means >=: equality is sufficient. Separate demand from available acceleration.

sweep.units: Speed V in m/s; initial pitch acceleration in rad/s².

experience.scenario: The trainer needs to begin pitching nose-up at 20 m/s. Its elevator must overcome a nose-down moment and achieve an initial angular acceleration of at least 0.12 rad/s².
experience.task: Write a question naming the aircraft condition, elevator, measured initial response and minimum requirement. You are defining success, not calculating a new target.
experience.method: Use the frame: At [condition], can [control] produce [response] of at least [requirement]? Initial angular acceleration is a change in rotation rate, not pitch angle or takeoff distance. Equality meets a minimum requirement.
experience.investigate: Compare the trainer at 20, 14 and 10 m/s. Which conditions meet the initial acceleration demand, and why can this not answer whether the aircraft takes off safely?
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.
